title: Research Results Presentation – Research Student Exchange Program Strengthening Academic and Cultural Ties between UGM and Kyushu University Japan
excerpt: Yogyakarta, March 19, 2025. An important milestone has been achieved in international research cooperation between Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) and Kyushu University, Japan. body:
**Yogyakarta, March 19, 2025.** An important milestone has been achieved in international research cooperation between Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) and Kyushu University, Japan. The culmination of this partnership was marked by the final presentation of Machika Shimizu, an exchange research student from Kyushu University, held at the Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (TPB), Faculty of Agricultural Technology (FTP) UGM. The research program ran from February 21 to March 26, 2025, as a follow-up to the Summer Course organized by UGM's Faculty of Forestry in 2024.

Under the guidance of Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho, Shimizu developed a plant health monitoring system using image processing and multispectral cameras. This innovative system was tested at the Laboratory of Environmental Engineering and Agricultural Buildings (TLBP) and the Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC) at FTP UGM. The system has the potential to detect diseases and nutrient deficiencies early, which can significantly increase agricultural productivity.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-1-exchange-research-jpn-19-at-16.39.33-1-1024x768.webp)

Final Presentation – Research Student Exchange

The application of Internet of Things (IoT) technology enables remote monitoring and efficient data analysis, which is crucial for modern agriculture. This research not only contributes to advances in agricultural technology but also aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) aimed at increasing agricultural productivity and sustainability.

The presentation was attended by prominent figures including Prof. Dr. Ir. Lilik Sutiarso (Head of Department TPB), Dr. Arifin Dwi Saputro (Secretary of Department TPB), Dr. Murtiningrum, Ardan Wiratmoko, M.Sc., Dr. Dwi Ayuni, Dr. Joko Nugroho, and Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho. Furthermore, research students from SARC and students attending Japanese language classes at the Faculty of Agriculture and FTP were also present, demonstrating the collaborative spirit of this program.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-2-exchange-research-jpn-at-14.01.12.webp)

Receiving a visit from SUIJI students at Smart Agri Plant Factory

Prof. Lilik Sutiarso emphasized the importance of sustaining this student exchange program as an initiative for cooperation between TPB Department UGM and the Faculty of Agriculture at Kyushu University. He highlighted that collaborations such as this are essential for promoting innovation in agricultural practice and enhancing educational experiences for students.

Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho added that this program not only focuses on research but also promotes cultural exchange and enhances foreign language proficiency among UGM students. Shimizu actively participated in various departmental activities, including assisting with the ASIIN accreditation visit from external assessors, receiving visits from Japanese students from the SUIJI program, attending a joint iftar at the Laboratory of Energy and Agricultural Machinery, Japanese language classes, and field visits to the Low-cost Smart Greenhouse in Sriharjo.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-3-lab-activity.webp)

Activities participated in by Machika Shimizu

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-4-cultural-activity-exchange-research.webp)

Cultural activities participated in by Machika Shimizu during her stay in Yogyakarta

The success of this program demonstrates the great potential of international collaboration in advancing smart agricultural technology in Indonesia. This reflects the shared commitment of UGM and Kyushu University to developing research and education as well as academic cultural exchange.

This cooperation was facilitated by Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho (UGM), Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D., and Assoc. Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara, Ph.D. (Kyushu University). The results of this research are expected to provide significant contributions to the agricultural sector, increasing productivity and sustainability in accordance with the SDGs.

original.body:
**Yogyakarta, 19 Maret 2025.** Sebuah tonggak penting dicapai dalam kerjasama riset internasional antara Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) dan Universitas Kyushu, Jepang. Puncak dari kemitraan ini ditandai dengan presentasi akhir Machika Shimizu, mahasiswa exchange research dari Universitas Kyushu, yang diadakan di Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem (TPB), Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian (FTP) UGM. Program riset ini berlangsung dari 21 Februari hingga 26 Maret 2025, sebagai tindak lanjut dari Summer Course yang diselenggarakan oleh Fakultas Kehutanan UGM pada tahun 2024.

Di bawah bimbingan Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho, Shimizu mengembangkan sistem pemantauan kesehatan tanaman menggunakan image processing dan kamera multispektral. Sistem inovatif ini diuji coba di Laboratorium Teknik Lingkungan dan Bangunan Pertanian (TLBP) dan Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC) di FTP UGM. Sistem ini memiliki potensi untuk mendeteksi penyakit dan kekurangan nutrisi secara dini, yang secara signifikan dapat meningkatkan produktivitas pertanian.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-1-exchange-research-jpn-19-at-16.39.33-1-1024x768.webp)

Presentasi Akhir – Research Student Exchange

Penerapan teknologi Internet of Things (IoT) memungkinkan pemantauan jarak jauh dan analisis data yang efisien, yang sangat penting untuk pertanian modern. Riset ini tidak hanya berkontribusi pada kemajuan teknologi pertanian tetapi juga sejalan dengan Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (SDGs) yang bertujuan untuk meningkatkan produktivitas pertanian dan keberlanjutan.

Presentasi tersebut dihadiri oleh tokoh-tokoh terkemuka termasuk Prof. Dr. Ir. Lilik Sutiarso (Ketua Departemen TPB), Dr. Arifin Dwi Saputro (Sekretaris Departemen TPB), Dr. Murtiningrum, Ardan Wiratmoko, M.Sc., Dr. Dwi Ayuni, Dr. Joko Nugroho, dan Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho. Selain itu, mahasiswa peneliti dari SARC dan mahasiswa yang mengikuti kelas bahasa Jepang di Fakultas Pertanian dan FTP juga hadir, menunjukkan semangat kolaboratif dari program ini.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-2-exchange-research-jpn-at-14.01.12.webp)

Menerima kunjungan mahasiswa dari SUIJI di Smart Agri Plant Factory

Prof. Lilik Sutiarso menekankan pentingnya keberlanjutan program exchange student ini sebagai inisiasi kerjasama antara Departemen TPB UGM dan Fakultas Pertanian Universitas Kyushu. Ia menyoroti bahwa kolaborasi semacam ini sangat penting untuk mendorong inovasi dalam praktik pertanian dan meningkatkan pengalaman pendidikan bagi mahasiswa.

Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho menambahkan bahwa program ini tidak hanya berfokus pada riset tetapi juga mempromosikan pertukaran budaya dan meningkatkan kemampuan berbahasa asing di kalangan mahasiswa UGM. Shimizu aktif berpartisipasi dalam berbagai kegiatan departemen, termasuk mendampingi visitasi ASIIN dari asesor luar negeri, menerima kunjungan mahasiswa Jepang dari program SUIJI, mengikuti buka puasa bersama di Laboratorium Energi dan Mesin Pertanian, kelas bahasa Jepang, dan kunjungan lapangan ke Low-cost Smart Greenhouse di Sriharjo.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-3-lab-activity.webp)

Kegiatan yang diikuti oleh Machika Shimizu

![](/brand/uploads/notes/334-4-cultural-activity-exchange-research.webp)

Aktivitas budaya yang diikuti oleh Machika Shimizu selama di Yogyakarta

Keberhasilan program ini menunjukkan potensi besar kolaborasi internasional dalam memajukan teknologi pertanian cerdas di Indonesia. Ini mencerminkan komitmen bersama UGM dan Universitas Kyushu dalam mengembangkan riset dan pendidikan serta pertukaran budaya akademik.

Kerjasama ini difasilitasi oleh Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho (UGM), Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D., dan Assoc. Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara, Ph.D. (Universitas Kyushu). Hasil dari riset ini diharapkan dapat memberikan kontribusi signifikan bagi sektor pertanian, meningkatkan produktivitas dan keberlanjutan sesuai dengan SDGs.
